history.summary: A white-marble Radha-Krishna temple complex at Jalan Nagar, just outside the campus of Assam Medical College and Hospital, about 1.8 km from Dibrugarh railway station. Named after the Jalan family - prominent Upper Assam tea planters and entrepreneurs from the early twentieth century, whose estate lands gave Jalan Nagar its name. The complex holds four to five white shrines amid gardens and lawns: the main Radha-Krishna shrine plus subsidiary shrines to Shiva, Durga and Hanuman; a Shiva shrine under a tree bears a signboard claiming Lord Shiva's shadow appeared there (local tradition - verify). The temple is prized for its calm, green setting and is a popular quiet retreat for residents, visitors and medical-college students. Construction date is not documented (verify).

name: Radha Krishna Mandir (Jalan Mandir)
town_description: Dibrugarh, the 'Tea City of India', is the largest city of Upper Assam on the banks of the Brahmaputra, about 440 km east of Guwahati. It is a major centre of the tea, oil and gas industries and a gateway to sights such as the Bogibeel bridge, Jokai Botanical Garden and the Ahom-era monuments of the district.

travel.road: In Jalan Nagar near Assam Medical College, off Convoy Road / AMC Road; city autos and taxis.
